clue.text: For auditor to check its box, diamonds pass dealer here?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the phrase before it is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to tick it off is to put a check in its box on a list
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card game: diamonds are led, someone passes, and the dealer is checked by an auditor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant ticking boxes, but it signals sound: 'tick it off' said aloud gives the first word and the start of the second; ICE completes it. The bridge words 'pass' and 'dealer' are the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A booking booth is where passes, that is tickets, are sold, so it is a place a pass dealer works.

clue.text: Russian vehicle going up a gear, stretched by run out

indicators.note: the reversed pieces are stretched to take in the cricket abbreviation
in a down clue going up means reading upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A Russian car changes up a gear, slowed by running out of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up' reads the gear phrase upwards as TIKA in this down clue; 'stretched by' opens that after its first letter for the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian carriage drawn by three horses abreast is a traditional vehicle of that country.

clue.text: One may plunge away, sealing leak up in company time

indicators.note: the reversed group goes in between company and time
in a down clue up means the letters read in reverse
the word for away encloses the word for leak

parts.note: off means away, as in going off
to take a leak or pee is to urinate

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks away during company time for a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plunge' suggests diving, but a cafetiere has a plunger. 'Sealing' makes OPEEFF, which 'up' turns into FFEEPO; 'in' puts that between the company and time abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafetiere is a brewing jug whose plunger is pushed down, so it is one item that may plunge.

clue.text: How you may regard mum or dad's bet

definitions.text: How you may regard mum or dad
definitions.meaning: words like mum and dad read the same in both directions
a wager on a horse to win or be placed

explanation.surface: Thinking about how a parent views a flutter on the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A wager split between a win and a place is the standard racing sense; palindromes read alike from either end.

clue.text: Pedal around quiet branch

indicators.note: the phrase for pedal goes around the word for quiet

parts.note: pedal as an adjective means relating to the foot, so it reads as 'of foot'
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A cyclist pedals softly round a quiet branch line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedal' looks like a noun or verb, but it is the adjective, from Latin pes, meaning 'of the foot'; 'around' wraps that phrase about the call for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A side growth from a plant's stem is a branch, and figuratively a subsidiary arm of an organisation.

clue.text: After a fix, John may be stimulated by hit

definitions.text: After a fix, John may be
definitions.meaning: john is slang for a toilet; once repaired its cistern works again
elated after a triumph or hit

explanation.surface: A drug user named John, high after a fix and a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' and 'hit' suggest drugs and 'John' a man, but john is a lavatory, which after mending flushes properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated and excited by a triumph is the idiomatic sense; the toilet reading takes it literally.

clue.text: See 5
In the firing line, Rex Brown, rather yellow

indicators.note: the abbreviation for king goes in the darts line

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players throw from
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Rex Brown is in the firing line for being rather cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rex Brown' reads as a name and 'yellow' as cowardly; the oche is the line in darts behind which a player stands to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: This earth pigment is a brownish yellow, so it is a brown leaning towards yellow.

clue.text: Loony stayed with us for periods at regular intervals

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters are rearranged madly

explanation.surface: A madman has moved in with us for the occasional spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular weekday comes round every seven days, so those days recur at fixed intervals.

clue.text: See 1
Of use in plot, is it heard from The Laughing Cavalier?

indicators.note: the question asks whether this is what one would hear, so the words are to be taken by sound

parts.note: The Laughing Cavalier is by the Dutch painter Frans Hals, so his laugh would be a Dutch 'ho'

explanation.surface: A playful question about whether a famous painting has any use in a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Laughing Cavalier is a Dutch portrait; a Dutchman's laugh, 'ho', sounds like the garden tool. 'Plot' is a vegetable plot, not a story.
explanation.definitionFit: This push-type weeding tool is used in a garden plot or allotment, hence useful there.

clue.text: Look out to the west, I'm alarmed by women in the area

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the exclamation is turned round

parts.note: eek is the cry of someone alarmed

indicators.note: the abbreviation for women is put inside the word for area

parts.note: a patch is an area, as in someone's own patch

explanation.surface: Someone looking west is alarmed to find women in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look out' seems to be a command to the alarmed speaker, but it is the definition; EEK reversed gives KEE, then W goes into PATCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To look out is to be on guard and observant, which is what a sentry or lookout does.

clue.text: Jauntily playing the Blues? (Hint: Article 4's involved)

indicators.note: the hint, article and number are wrapped up inside the Blues

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservative party, whose members are Tories
an inkling is a hint
the is the definite article
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone cheerfully playing blues music, with a bracketed tip about article 4.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Blues' looks like music, but blue is the British Conservative colour, so TORIES; a Tory is a member of that party.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivories are piano keys, so playing them lightly is jaunty piano playing.

clue.text: In education, soldiers present and correct

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed in the abbreviation for education

parts.note: men is a general word for soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A military parade report: soldiers in training, present and correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present and correct' is a stock phrase for a roll call; here 'present and' only links, and 'correct' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct a text is to revise it and remove errors, the usual sense of the verb.

clue.text: Parker may need to verify credentials of messenger, with talk going about and getting spread

indicators.note: going about means turning round, so the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a DNA test verifies a person's identity; DNA is the molecule whose message is carried by messenger RNA
to yap is to talk noisily
a display is a spread laid out to be seen

explanation.surface: A courier has his credentials checked while gossip circulates about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parker' is one who parks a car, not a person's name; in the UK this sign means buy a ticket and show it on the dashboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver leaving a car in a ticketed bay must buy a voucher and leave it visible on the dashboard.

clue.text: Lumberjack's timekeeping under discussion? It shows the necessary power

indicators.note: something being discussed is spoken, so the phrase is to be heard

parts.note: a lumberjack would log a rhythm, keeping time

explanation.surface: Discussing how a lumberjack keeps time while chopping.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths this value is the exponent to which a base must be raised to give a number, the power needed.

clue.text: Tell me the reason for appeal to the men in white coats

definitions.text: appeal to the men in white coats
definitions.meaning: the cricket fielders' call to the umpires, who wear white coats

explanation.surface: A plea to doctors or asylum attendants for an explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men in white coats' suggests psychiatric staff; in cricket the umpires wear white coats and fielders appeal to them for a wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a colloquial request for explanation and the formal cricket appeal for a dismissal.

clue.text: Having the edge on, say, Iago's house and home, joining excursion

definitions.text: Having the edge on, say, Iago

indicators.note: the house and home go into the trip, joining it in the middle

parts.note: an outing is an excursion
a villa is a house
in means at home

explanation.surface: Iago's house and home are described as joining a day trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' after Iago makes him seem to own the house; it means 'has' in the definition, Iago being Shakespeare's arch-villain in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more wicked than a famous schemer like Iago is surpassing him in villainy, to out-Herod Herod in Shakespeare's style.

clue.text: See 12
Swapping couples having ailment to confront that's inclined to be frigid

indicators.note: two pairs of letters change places between the two words

parts.note: ill means an ailment
to face is to confront

explanation.surface: Partners swapping lead to an awkward ailment to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapping couples' is exact: in ILL FACE the pair LL and the pair CE trade places, giving ICE FALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep, broken section of glacier is frozen and sloping, hence frigid and inclined.

clue.text: Trojan horse finally gains access to a stable when mounted

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means raised up, so the letters read upwards
the last letter gets inside the word for stable

parts.note: sane means mentally stable

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word horse

explanation.surface: The wooden horse at Troy finally gets into a stable when ridden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trojan horse' looks like one phrase; 'horse' belongs to the wordplay. SANE takes E and A follows, then all is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of Virgil's Aeneid was a prince of Troy, so he is a Trojan.

clue.text: Fleece stolen most recently from back row

indicators.note: reading from the back means the remaining letters are taken in reverse
to fleece is to strip, here stripping the outside letters off

parts.note: hot means stolen, so the most recently stolen goods are the hottest

explanation.surface: A sheep's fleece has been stolen from the back row, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like the stolen item, but it means stripping the ends from HOTTEST, leaving OTTES, which 'from back' turns round. 'Row' rhymes with 'cow', not 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A row in the sense of quarrel or scrap is a fight or argument.

clue.text: Quite fancy the end together

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rather likes the ending together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite fancy' reads as 'rather like'; 'Quite' is the definition and 'fancy' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Quite means completely, and doing something to an extreme extent is the idiomatic meaning of the phrase.

clue.text: See 22
Height's the attraction of the Tower of Pisa — people on them will have to go

definitions.text: people on them will have to go

parts.note: it means sex appeal or attraction
the leaning tower lists, that is it tilts

explanation.surface: Height is what draws visitors to the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' links: what the Tower of Pisa does is lean, i.e. it lists.
explanation.definitionFit: These are rosters of targets to be eliminated, so people named there are marked for removal.

clue.text: To make things worse, one's following subjects around the Sunshine State

parts.note: a fan is one who follows a team or star

indicators.note: the subjects go around the state abbreviation

parts.note: themes are subjects
Florida is the Sunshine State, abbreviated FLA

explanation.surface: A follower's interests revolve around Florida.
explanation.walkthrough: FLA is the older abbreviation for Florida, nicknamed the Sunshine State; it splits THEMES as THE...MES.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeding a fire air makes it burn harder, an idiom for aggravating a dispute or bad situation.

clue.text: Facial hair this man's put inside urn

indicators.note: the words for this man are placed inside the facial hair

parts.note: tashes is short for moustaches
he refers to this man

explanation.surface: A man stuffs his shaved-off facial hair into an urn.
explanation.walkthrough: The urn is the small trophy for which England and Australia play Test cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket trophy contested by England and Australia is a tiny urn, so the urn names the series.
